reasoning_notes.reasoning: With no history and no payroll cost advantage to matching, wage 0 earns the full 20 if C bids above 0; bidding higher only gives away profit. If C also bids 0, I still earn 10 from the tie.
With no history, choose a midpoint wage to balance the chance of winning labor against the margin earned if I do.
C bid 10 and won; matching earns 5 if tied, while a higher bid reduces margin. With an unknown horizon, match its observed bid.
I won at 10, earning 10. With no evidence A will change its zero bid, repeating 10 preserves a profitable win; undercutting would only reduce profit.
Matching C’s last bid preserves a chance at half the labor while avoiding a costly raise; the horizon is unknown.

C has bid 10 every round, including after I matched and undercut it. Matching gives half the labor and profit 5; bidding below loses, while bidding above costs more for the same half share.
